title: rulecad assembly
description: Objects placed together: a fit check (fits between them, joints and poses) or a plate (everything printed at once).

packed.description: Written by cad plates: which assembly this plate is for, its filament and gap, and each part's build hash, so a changed part re-packs only its plate

fasten.description: Screwed joints: each names its screw, the parts it passes through in order, and the part it ends in. The holes are read from the parts as drawn and each screw followed along one axis; a fasten holds its parts as a fit that fastens does, lines their holes up as a holes fit does, and puts its screws on the shopping list. Draw the holes with v.fixings, and name the screw with no length: the check chooses one

joins.description: How beams are joined: each names an end of one beam (a) and a place on another (b), and its kind. A join puts its operations on both beams (a tap in a's end, an access or clearance hole across b), its screws into fasten, and a spring for the frame's solve; join.geometry checks the end meets the face square and flush where b says

defaultSnippets.label: join
defaultSnippets.description: A blind join: a's end tapped, its screw's head in b's slot

task.description: What the machine is for: the tool, where it works, how fast and how accurately

deflection.description: mm of link deflection at the tool, an estimate; else worked out from the parts when there is a payload

grip.description: A compliant gripper on a servo: { servo, horn, leaf: { length, thickness, width }, travel, friction, lever, margin }

pen.description: Servo angles for the pen: { up, down }

gait.description: Poses in time: the feet by anchor, a pattern, and the body

wires.description: Wires between anchors, their length measured through every pose

via.description: Anchors or path joints the wire is routed by

current.description: A: else a motor's rated current at either end, or a signal's

gravity.description: Which way down is, for masses in loads (default [0, 0, -1])

loads.description: What the assembly has to do: a torque (N m) or force (N) on a joint, or a mass (kg) carried at an anchor

poses.description: Named sets of joint values ({ "hinge": 90 }), and of items' variables ("action.travel": 25: a flexure drawn bent in that pose, printed as drawn)

motor.description: A motor from @rulecad/motors: bought, not printed; its shaft turns the joint it drives

set.description: Figures that differ from the catalogue's, by name

speed.description: The motor's speed, rpm (default: what it does comfortably)

margin.description: How many times over the torque must be (default 2)

duty.description: The share of the time it runs, 0 to 1 (default 1), for its heat

screw.description: The screws through a motor's plain holes, if not the size they take: M3

driver.description: The bought driver item this motor plugs into

stiffness.description: N per mm of strain, per mm of belt width

current.description: A per coil, as set on the driver (default its rated current)

cooled.description: The driver has a heat sink and moving air

microsteps.description: Steps to a full step (default 16): resolution, not accuracy

bought.description: A part from a rule set ("608", "drv8825"): bought, not printed; drawn faint from its figures, with anchors from what it is

fitting.description: A printed fitting from @rulecad/frames, drawn from a profile's and its slot nuts' rules and sized from a named load (a join with "fitting": "printed" adds one for itself; a panel adds its clips, a door its hinges, handle and catch). A bracket, gusset or splice is sized by finite elements; the others by beam formulas, each reporting its grams and margin. In its fitted frame: a bracket's x along b's face away from a, y up a, z across; a plate's x along b, y along a, its contact face at z = 0

profile.description: The profile the base leg or the plate lies on

other.description: A bracket's: the profile its upright leg lies on, where not the same

face.description: The face of the profile it lies on (top, top.2): its slot sizes the tongue and the nut

brace.description: A bracket's brace across its inside corner

load.description: The design load in N, across beam a at the fitting's screw (default 100)

count.description: A plate's screws on each arm (default 2)

part.description: A hinge's leaf (frame, door) or a levelling foot's part (body, pad): an item each

sheet.description: The panel's or door's thickness, in mm

standoff.description: A latch's or catch's: the door's inner face over the beam's face (a hinge's standoff)

panel.description: A panel from @rulecad/frames: a sheet cut to the bay of four beams it closes, on their faces that look along out, held by printed clips at a pitch; with door, a door on printed hinges that turns on a joint

bay.description: The four beam items round it, in order

out.description: The way its face looks, square to the bay

hinge.description: The beam of the bay its hinges go on

beam.description: A length of a profile from @rulecad/frames: bought and cut to length, faint in previews; placed by its ends (from, to, roll) or by at and rotate

profile.description: A profile's name: 2020-misumi-hfs5, profile-4040-item-8, or a set in this workspace's rules/

length.description: mm from end a to end b; may be left out when from and to are both given

printed.description: A printed beam (a later release): a bought one is false, the default

material.description: A material set in place of the profile's alloy: al6063-t5, or a plastic

ops.description: Operations on the beam, each a line on its sheet and a cut in its solid, placed by an address on the beam and dimensioned from end a

to.description: A beam's end b, with from its end a

roll.description: Degrees a beam placed by its ends turns about its own axis, a toward b; at 0 its top faces up (+z), or +y when it stands upright

from.description: For a beam: its end a, [x, y, z]. For an object: inputs worked out from items built before it, { input: expression }

engage.description: a goes at least this far (mm) onto b along the joint between them: a part slid onto a shaft or a pin, not resting on its end

radius.description: With engage: how near the joint's axis to look (mm, default 10)

shaft.description: a or b is a motor, and the other takes its shaft: reads the bore from the part as drawn

seat.description: a or b is a bought bearing, and the other its printed seat: reads the pocket as drawn against the bearing's rules and the printer's fit (fit.seat)

fastens.description: a and b are fastened together (pins, a press, a clip): what holds a part that has no joint. Where screws hold them, use a fasten instead: it knows the screw, checks its holes and lists it

fastener.description: What does the fastening, by hand (two push pins): named on the shopping list and the assembly step. A screw is a fasten's, which chooses its length and counts it

access.description: <item>.<anchor>: where the screw's tool comes from, its z axis pointing out along the screw. Whatever stands on that line goes on after the screw; if nothing can, assembly.order says so

holes.description: A holes fit: a circuit board's part (pcb.board) whose mounting holes are followed down into the part named by into. Where the board is screwed there, a fasten with "holes" says it and knows the screw: cad check suggests it, cad add fasten --from-fits writes it

depth.description: With holes: how far each screw's path must be clear (mm)

direction.description: With holes: up for screws from below

ring.description: With holes: how far round each screw there must be material (mm, default the hole's diameter)

into.description: With holes: the part the screws go into

within.description: With an anchor name (item@anchor): only faces this close to it (mm, default 10)

beamAddress.description: An address on a beam, without its item: an end (a, b), an end's bore (a.1), or a face's place with a distance from end a (top@120), from end b (top@-20) or a share of the length (top@50%), the second place of a face top.2@120

beamOp.description: An operation on a beam (@rulecad/frames OPS): each takes only its own keys, and is refused by name otherwise

op.description: cut: square to length; mitre: an end at an angle about a named face; tap: a thread in an end bore; access: a hole across, in line with a slot, for a key; drill: through one wall or right through, plain or tapped; counterbore: a seat for a head; pocket: milled by outline; notch: a slot's lips cut away; deburr: named so the sheet asks for it

thread.description: A thread by name (M5): sizes the hole, the tap or the seat through @rulecad/fixings

head.description: A counterbore's head: cap, button, hex or pan

diameter.description: mm, in place of a thread's figure

depth.description: mm from the face or the end

through.description: A drilled hole through one wall (the default) or right through the beam

angle.description: A mitre's angle from square, degrees

about.description: The face a mitre's angle is seen on

long.description: The side a mitred beam's length is measured on

outline.description: A pocket's outline, points [along, across] about the address

length.description: A notch's length along the beam, mm

address.description: An anchor by name, <item>.<anchor>; on a beam an end (x1.a, x1.b), an end bore (x1.a.1), or a face with a distance from end a (x1.top@120), from end b (x1.top@-20) or a share of the length (x1.top@50%), the second slot of a face x1.top.2@120

join.description: Two beams joined: an end of one (a), a place on the other (b), and how (kind)

kind.description: blind: a's end tapped, a button-head screw's head in b's slot, an access hole across b. end-tap: a's end tapped, a cap screw through a hole drilled across b. bracket, gusset and splice with "fitting": "printed" add a printed fitting and its screws. The rest are checked where they meet and stiffen the frame by an estimate; their fittings come in later releases

a.description: A beam's end: y1.a, or one bore of it where the end has several (y1.a.2)

b.description: A place on the other beam where a's end (its bore's axis) meets it: a face with a distance from its end a (x1.back@120, x1.top@-20, x1.top@50%), or an end (x1.b) for a splice, mitre or corner

fitting.description: For a kind with a fitting: printed or bought. Printed, a bracket, gusset or splice join adds the fitting as an item, placed from where the beams are, its screws into slot nuts in both beams as fastens, and its own stiffness by finite elements

brace.description: A printed bracket's brace across its inside corner

load.description: A printed fitting's design load in N, across beam a at its screw (default 100): it is sized to about twice the margin at it

nut.description: A printed fitting's slot nuts' kind (default: the strongest made for the slot)

screw.description: For blind and end-tap: the screw by thread and head (M5 button), where not the end bore's thread with the kind's head

fasten.description: A screwed joint: the screw by thread and head, the parts it passes in order, the part it ends in, and where the screws go (at, an anchor each, or holes, a part's own holes)

defaultSnippets.label: screws in a part's own holes

screw.description: The screw, by its thread and head: M3 cap, M4 button, M3x12 countersunk, 6-32 UNC cap (the names @rulecad/fixings reads). With no length in the name, the shortest sold length that fits is chosen

through.description: The parts the screw passes through, in order from under its head: items (bracket) or item.part (bracket.body). Each needs a clearance hole for the thread

into.description: The part the screw ends in: a pilot, a tapped or printed thread, an insert's hole or a nut's seat there, or a clearance hole with nut. Or a slot on a beam (x1.top, x1.top.2, x1.top@120): the screw ends in a slot nut under the slot's lips, the one made for that slot and thread (nut chooses its kind), and each screw lies over a slot's centre line (fasten.slot)

at.description: One screw at each anchor: a point on its axis (bracket.h1), the anchor's axis along the screw

holes.description: In place of at: a part whose holes are the screws' places, found in the part as drawn (a circuit board: its mounting holes)

nut.description: What holds the screw where the part it ends in does not: true or hex, square, lock. It sits on that part's far face, or in a nut's seat drawn there. Into a beam's slot, the slot nut's kind: slide-in, drop-in, roll-in, hammer, square or t-bolt (left out, the strongest made for the slot). A slide-in or square nut enters only from an open end of the slot (frame.nut, frame.preload)

washer.description: A plain washer under the head

length.description: The screw's length in mm, where the name gives none: checked for reaching, bottoming out and standing proud

torque.description: The tightening torque, N m: the pressure under the head is then held against the material it sits on (fasten.seat)

support.description: What takes this joint's tipping load: bought bearings, or printed clips (read by FE)

pitch.description: Diameter the clips stand on, mm

errors.description: What this joint adds to the error at the tool, degrees, by name (play, twist, bearing): an expression reading a rule, so a measurement moves it

brake.description: What holds this joint with the power off (a ratchet, a detent): counted by motor.holds

mesh.description: Gears: this joint's gear meshes with the gear on the joint named by with, which drives it

planetary.description: A planetary gearbox: one of sun, carrier and ring held, the one named by drive turning, the rest following it in phase

output.description: A compound planetary: a second ring, on the planets' second step
